newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Soft on weak swaps, poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Soft on weak swaps, poor demand.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was stable to slightly softer on Tuesday amid weak fuel oil swaps and slack China demand, traders said.
A Japanese trader bought two 20,000-tonne cargoes from two majors at $99 and $98.5 per tonne for April 5-9 and April 6-10 lifting, traders said.
"I think the prices are pretty all right for a slow market like this," said one trader.
"The overall market should be weaker because Japanese are not major buyers and the Chinese are still away," the trader said, noting ample supplies.
Traders have been offering cargoes, and lowering down their prices, since last Friday but could not find buyers.
Offers for the 180-cst grade slid to Monday's $99 per tonne from Friday's $101.
Fuel oil swaps continued a recent downtrend, with March last quoted at $97.00/$98.50 per tonne compared with Monday's $98.25/$99.20.
April swaps were unchanged at $95.50/$96.50.
"There are only few enquiries and it seems demand may continue decreasing," said one trader.
Overnight losses in crude values further added gloom to the slow market, traders said.
Anticipation that some March maintenance turnarounds in Singapore might take away some stocks and could support prices, they said. But might not be able to boost sentiment, they added.
"Many people stay away from the market because there has not been enough physical activities to indicate directions," said another trader.
